sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Platform setup and run tasks
sections.what: Sets the runtime tools and deployment type, defines the Run button workflow with its two validation checks, names the post-merge script, and lists system packages.
sections.why: Likely reason: the hosting platform needs these settings to build and start the project. The file does not say more.
sections.watch_out: The post-merge time limit is four minutes. A long data replay can hit that limit before it finishes.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Port mapping
sections.what: Maps three internal ports to public ports 80, 3001, and 3000.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: exposes the web app and the API to the outside.
sections.watch_out: The internal ports must match what the app actually listens on, or the site will be unreachable.

summary: Configuration for the Replit hosting environment. It sets which tools to install, what the Run button starts, which ports are exposed, and which script runs after a merge.
purpose: Tells the hosting platform how to set up and run this project.
why: The purpose is platform setup. The reason for each individual choice is not stated in the file.
how: Lists the runtime tools, the deployment type, and a post-build cleanup step. Defines a Run workflow that runs two validation scripts in parallel. Sets agent settings, the post-merge script with a four-minute time limit, system packages, and three port mappings to public ports.
outputs: The prepared environment, the tasks started by the Run button, and the exposed ports.
risks: The Run button depends on two validation scripts that check data baselines, so they can fail when data is missing. The post-merge time limit of four minutes may cut off a long data replay. A wrong port mapping makes the site unreachable.
debug: If the Run button fails, check the two validation scripts it names. If merge setup times out, read the post-merge messages and compare against the time limit. If the site is unreachable, check the port mappings against the ports the app uses.
